synopsis: Terrain-edge hazards dominate the cited US surface-mining fatality analysis: of 54 haul-truck deaths from January 2005 to June 2021, 21 involved berms and 12 dump points, versus 13 involving people or vehicles; 10 of the 12 dump-point cases involved an absent or inadequate berm [f2989, f2998, f3000]. This exposes a mismatch with research focused on vehicle-to-vehicle collisions: object detection alone covers an incomplete risk picture, and berm or dump-edge prevention may also require road-edge, geofence, speed and stability controls [f6577, f11511, f3250]. Berm handling must be context-aware rather than brake for every berm or learn away repeated dump-edge alarms; the glossary's claim that using berms as bump stops is safe is qualified by two fatal cases where repeated bumping pushed the berm toward the edge [f11512, f3353, f3354, f11864, f3351]. Virtual validation needs accurately located edges because errors of tens of centimetres can corrupt stopping-distance tests, while terrain editing in Gaussian scenes and realistic terrain reproduction by the discussed over-the-air devices remain gaps [f3910, f3880, f5327]. Representation should distinguish structured haul roads from unstructured terrain: OpenDRIVE is recommended for structured road elements, but lane-free haul-road suitability remains a gap and dig faces, stockpiles and free terrain require additional representations [f3982, f7158, f7202, f13216].
